goal: After a fixed bound of consecutive cycles that make no progress on a unit (a phase whose verify never passes, or an autopilot repo that never authors a task), the re-driver backs that unit off and routes it to the human-review queue with a no-progress reason instead of re-running it the next cycle.

relevant: packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- the phase_verify path (~993) that keeps a fully-DONE phase active forever when verify never passes
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_autopilot.py -- the discovery loop that re-runs full discovery every cycle for an un-authorable repo
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_orchestrate.py -- the loop where per-unit no-progress cycles are counted and backed off / routed to the queue surface
constraints: Count consecutive no-progress cycles per unit; after a fixed bound, back the unit off (do NOT re-attempt it the next cycle) and route it to the queue with a machine-readable no-progress reason (criteria #9, #13)
Progress definition is observable (a state change / a task authored / a verify passing); a backed-off unit must be absent from the active set on the cycle after the bound is crossed
The bound is finite so a never-progressing unit cannot burn agent cost forever; commit before reporting done
non_goals: Do not modify files under packages/*/tests/; do not weaken or delete assertions
Do not change phase_verify or autopilot discovery semantics themselves -- only add the bounded no-progress back-off + routing around them
edge_cases: A unit that DOES make progress resets its no-progress counter and is never backed off
Back-off must produce exactly one queue entry per backed-off unit, not a re-queue every cycle
